content: The label will be provided in English, and translations into other official languages will be developed in collaboration with regional and country offices. The recommendations and supporting information will be incorporated into the WHO HIV Treatment App 2, a free mobile application designed for easy access and reference. This app is available globally for download on major app stores. Additionally, printed materials, PDFs, and social media links will be made available to disseminate key messages from WHO recommendations. Key annexes containing systematic reviews and other supporting information will be uploaded to the WHO website. Derivative products, such as slide sets, Q&A documents, and webinars with key stakeholders, will be created to assist countries in adapting and implementing the guidelines within their specific contexts. The Department of Global HIV, Viral Hepatitis, and Sexually Transmitted Infection Programmes monitors the adoption of HIV-related recommendations through mechanisms such as the Global AIDS Monitoring framework, country surveys, and population-based HIV impact assessments. These tools provide indirect evidence of the impact of WHO recommendations. The department will collaborate with WHO regional and country offices, major donors, and implementing partners to support the uptake and implementation of these guidelines. Potential barriers include delays in dissemination due to the time required for translation and limited resources in some countries, which may hinder the ability to update existing policies. Ongoing scoping reviews are conducted to anticipate future guidance needs. When necessary, rapid guidance and technical or operational updates will complement the guideline updates.
